review_cadence: monthly for time-sensitive figures; annually for survey findings
usage_rule: Use the claim, period, population, source and limitation together. Do not reuse a figure without its scope or convert an estimate into a census count.

evidence.claim: More than 3,380 single-family offices were operating in Hong Kong at the end of 2025.
evidence.population_or_sample: Market estimate of single-family offices operating in Hong Kong
evidence.publisher: Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau and Invest Hong Kong
evidence.source_title: Hong Kong's single-family offices total surpasses 3 380, injecting over $10 billion annually into local economy
evidence.source_type: Official HKSAR Government release reporting an InvestHK-commissioned Deloitte market study
evidence.limitation: This is a commissioned market estimate, not a registry or census. The public release does not disclose the 2025 study's sample, model or confidence interval. [needs source: full 2025 methodology]

evidence.claim: Hong Kong's estimated single-family-office population increased by about 680, or more than 25%, over the two years to the end of 2025.
evidence.population_or_sample: Comparison of Deloitte market estimates for Hong Kong single-family offices
evidence.publisher: Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau and Invest Hong Kong
evidence.source_title: Hong Kong's single-family offices total surpasses 3 380, injecting over $10 billion annually into local economy
evidence.source_type: Official HKSAR Government release reporting an InvestHK-commissioned Deloitte market study
evidence.limitation: The comparison is between market estimates. It must not be described as registrations, incorporations or government-facilitated offices. [needs source: full 2025 methodology]

evidence.claim: The commissioned study estimated that Hong Kong single-family offices contribute about HK$12.6 billion annually through operating expenditure alone.
evidence.population_or_sample: Estimated operating expenditure of single-family offices operating in Hong Kong
evidence.period: Estimate published 10 February 2026 using the end-2025 market study
evidence.publisher: Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau and Invest Hong Kong
evidence.source_title: Hong Kong's single-family offices total surpasses 3 380, injecting over $10 billion annually into local economy
evidence.source_type: Official HKSAR Government release reporting an InvestHK-commissioned Deloitte market study
evidence.limitation: This is an estimate of operating expenditure, not total investment, tax revenue, GDP contribution or assets under management. [needs source: full 2025 methodology]

evidence.claim: The commissioned study estimated that Hong Kong single-family offices directly employ more than 10,000 full-time professionals.
evidence.population_or_sample: Estimated direct employment within single-family-office operations in Hong Kong
evidence.period: Estimate published 10 February 2026 using the end-2025 market study
evidence.publisher: Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau and Invest Hong Kong
evidence.source_title: Hong Kong's single-family offices total surpasses 3 380, injecting over $10 billion annually into local economy
evidence.source_type: Official HKSAR Government release reporting an InvestHK-commissioned Deloitte market study
evidence.limitation: This is estimated direct full-time employment. It excludes wider service-provider employment and should not be described as a payroll census. [needs source: full 2025 methodology]

evidence.claim: Hong Kong's asset and wealth management business recorded HK$42.2 trillion in assets under management in 2025, up 20% year on year.
evidence.population_or_sample: 1,316 participating firms: relevant SFC-licensed corporations, banks, registered insurers and trustees
evidence.source_title: Hong Kong's AUM grew 20% to record high: SFC's 2025 survey on asset and wealth management
evidence.limitation: The survey excludes entities managing their own wealth that may not require an SFC licence, including single-family offices, sovereign wealth funds and endowments, and excludes direct HKSAR Government investments.

evidence.claim: Net fund inflows into Hong Kong's asset and wealth management business reached HK$2.1 trillion in 2025, up 193% year on year and rising for a third consecutive year.
evidence.population_or_sample: 1,316 participating firms in the SFC Asset and Wealth Management Activities Survey 2025
evidence.source_title: Hong Kong's AUM grew 20% to record high: SFC's 2025 survey on asset and wealth management
evidence.limitation: This is an industry-wide aggregate covered by the SFC survey, not a measure of flows into family offices or FOIHK.

evidence.claim: Private banking and private wealth management assets under management reached HK$12.9 trillion in 2025, up 24% year on year.
evidence.population_or_sample: Private banking and private wealth management segment within the SFC's 1,316-firm annual survey
evidence.source_title: Hong Kong's AUM grew 20% to record high: SFC's 2025 survey on asset and wealth management
evidence.limitation: This segment is not equivalent to the assets of Hong Kong family offices and must not be presented as such.

evidence.claim: The net asset value of SFC-authorised Hong Kong-domiciled funds reached HK$2.3 trillion at the end of 2025, up 38% year on year.
evidence.figure: HK$2.3 trillion NAV; +38% year on year
evidence.population_or_sample: SFC-authorised funds domiciled in Hong Kong
evidence.period: As at 31 December 2025 compared with 31 December 2024
evidence.source_title: Hong Kong's AUM grew 20% to record high: SFC's 2025 survey on asset and wealth management
evidence.source_type: Regulator survey and administrative fund data
evidence.limitation: This is the NAV of SFC-authorised Hong Kong-domiciled funds, not all funds sold in Hong Kong and not family-office AUM.

evidence.claim: More than 181,000 individual investors had participated in Cross-boundary Wealth Management Connect by the end of May 2026, with cumulative cross-boundary remittances above RMB138 billion.
evidence.population_or_sample: Administrative totals for Wealth Management Connect across Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao
evidence.publisher: Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau
evidence.source_title: LCQ22: Promoting mutual access in terms of asset and wealth management
evidence.source_type: Official HKSAR Government administrative programme data
evidence.limitation: Figures cover the whole cross-boundary programme and are not family-office-specific. Remittances include Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao flows.

evidence.claim: Hong Kong funds in the Mainland-Hong Kong Mutual Recognition of Funds arrangement recorded RMB82.5 billion of net subscriptions in the Mainland in 2025, 2.3 times the prior-year amount.
evidence.figure: RMB82.5 billion net subscriptions; 2.3 times year on year
evidence.population_or_sample: Hong Kong mutual recognition funds offered in the Mainland
evidence.publisher: Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau
evidence.source_title: LCQ22: Promoting mutual access in terms of asset and wealth management
evidence.source_type: Official HKSAR Government administrative market-access data
evidence.limitation: This measures net subscriptions to eligible mutual recognition funds in the Mainland, not all cross-border investment and not family-office flows.

evidence.claim: At 28 February 2026, the New Capital Investment Entrant Scheme had received 3,166 applications; 1,762 applicants had completed investment and received formal approval, and verified investment-requirement capital totalled HK$55.636 billion.
evidence.figure: 3,166 applications; 1,762 formal approvals; HK$55.636 billion verified capital
evidence.population_or_sample: All New CIES applications and verified investment-requirement capital recorded by InvestHK and the Immigration Department
evidence.publisher: Invest Hong Kong and the HKSAR Government
evidence.source_title: Two-year milestone: New Capital Investment Entrant Scheme attracts nearly 3 200 applications
evidence.limitation: The separately reported HK$95 billion was anticipated investment based on applications; it was not completed investment. Use HK$55.636 billion when discussing verified capital at this date.

evidence.claim: HKIMR's 2026 family-office study surveyed 101 entities and conducted 35 stakeholder interviews.
evidence.population_or_sample: 32 single-family offices, 23 multi-family offices, 20 UHNW individuals and 26 financial institutions; interviews also included academics, legal practitioners, government, impact organisations and NGOs
evidence.period: Survey December 2024 to April 2025; interviews October 2024 to April 2025
evidence.publisher: Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research
evidence.source_title: Beyond Wealth: Advancing Hong Kong's Family Office Ecosystem Through Philanthropy, Impact Investing, and Risk Management
evidence.limitation: The study is a stakeholder survey, not a census of Hong Kong family offices. Percentages in the report may use question-specific respondent subsets.

evidence.claim: In the HKIMR survey, 95% of respondents reported investment and asset management activity, 74% reported risk management, and roughly three quarters reported professional advisory activity.
evidence.figure: 95% investment and asset management; 74% risk management; about 75% professional advisory
evidence.population_or_sample: Relevant respondents within the 101-entity HKIMR survey
evidence.publisher: Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research
evidence.source_title: Beyond Wealth: Advancing Hong Kong's Family Office Ecosystem Through Philanthropy, Impact Investing, and Risk Management
evidence.limitation: The report presents percentages, but the executive material does not state the exact response count for each question. Cite the overall sample and avoid converting percentages into respondent counts. [needs source: question-level n for full provenance]

evidence.claim: Among surveyed family offices and UHNW individuals, 45% were active in philanthropy and 30% in impact investing; respondents expected these shares to reach 64% and 43% over the following three years.
evidence.figure: Philanthropy 45% current and 64% planned; impact investing 30% current and 43% planned
evidence.population_or_sample: Family-office and UHNW-individual respondents within the 101-entity HKIMR survey
evidence.period: Current activity reported during December 2024 to April 2025; intentions for the subsequent three years
evidence.publisher: Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research
evidence.source_title: Beyond Wealth: Advancing Hong Kong's Family Office Ecosystem Through Philanthropy, Impact Investing, and Risk Management
evidence.limitation: The future figures are respondent intentions, not forecasts or guaranteed outcomes. The exact question-level respondent count is not stated in the executive material. [needs source: question-level n for full provenance]

evidence.claim: HKIMR respondents reported current Hong Kong purchases of investment-related and non-investment risk products at 54% and 43%, with intended use over the next three years at 78% and 61%.
evidence.figure: Investment-risk products 54% current and 78% intended; non-investment risk products 43% current and 61% intended
evidence.population_or_sample: Relevant respondents within the 101-entity HKIMR survey
evidence.period: Current activity reported during December 2024 to April 2025; intentions for the subsequent three years
evidence.publisher: Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research
evidence.source_title: Beyond Wealth: Advancing Hong Kong's Family Office Ecosystem Through Philanthropy, Impact Investing, and Risk Management
evidence.limitation: The future figures describe intended purchases, not actual future demand. The exact question-level respondent count should be added before describing this as full-provenance evidence. [needs source: question-level n]

evidence.claim: In the HKIMR study, 83% of respondents said they had sufficient talent for daily operations, while the report also identified recruitment challenges in family-office-specific skills and career visibility.
evidence.figure: 83% reported sufficient talent for daily operations
evidence.population_or_sample: Relevant respondents within the 101-entity HKIMR survey
evidence.publisher: Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research
evidence.source_title: Beyond Wealth: Advancing Hong Kong's Family Office Ecosystem Through Philanthropy, Impact Investing, and Risk Management
evidence.limitation: Sufficient day-to-day talent does not mean there is no specialist skills gap. The exact question-level respondent count is not stated in the executive material. [needs source: question-level n]

evidence.claim: Hong Kong had 11,079 tax-exempt charities under section 88 at 31 March 2026; 412 were newly exempted and 205 had exemption status withdrawn during 2025/26.
evidence.population_or_sample: Inland Revenue Department administrative records for section 88 tax-exempt charities
evidence.source_title: IRD press release: tax-exempt charities statistics
evidence.limitation: This is the number of organisations holding section 88 tax exemption, not the number of all non-profit organisations, associations or companies limited by guarantee in Hong Kong. It does not establish FOIHK's own tax status.

evidence.claim: Hong Kong generally allows deductions for approved charitable donations up to 35% of assessable income or profits, subject to an aggregate minimum donation of HK$100 and statutory conditions.
evidence.population_or_sample: Hong Kong salaries tax, personal assessment and profits tax rules for approved charitable donations
evidence.period: Current Inland Revenue Department guidance verified 3 August 2026
evidence.limitation: Eligibility depends on the donor, recipient and statutory conditions. This is general information, not tax advice, and should not be used to imply that FOIHK is a section 88 charity.

needs_source.required_evidence: Dated internal membership register, clear counting rule and permission to publish the aggregate

needs_source.claim: Any statement about FOIHK event attendance, satisfaction, introductions, deals or participant outcomes
needs_source.required_evidence: Event registration or attendance records, survey instrument, response count, measurement period and publication consent

needs_source.claim: Named customer, member or partner endorsements and success stories
needs_source.required_evidence: Written approval, attributable name and title, date, context and substantiation for any numerical outcome

needs_source.claim: The sample, model and confidence interval behind the end-2025 estimate of more than 3,380 Hong Kong single-family offices
needs_source.required_evidence: Full 2025 Deloitte market-study methodology or technical appendix from Deloitte or InvestHK
